DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Who the Drum Is For

STS-HS10-L2-13001400-HSVPA910-CSR-AAD-01 • HS Theatre Grades 9–10 • Purpose and Intended Audience
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
A concert party never sold a ticket. The troupes loaded a van, drove to a market square in Ghana, and played for whoever was standing there: traders, children, people on their way home. Because the crowd was free to walk away, every choice in the show had to earn them, from the joke to the drumbeat to the ending. Amara's team is storyboarding The Talking Drum the same way, one panel at a time, with the market crowd in mind the whole time.
Look at the storyboard again. If the show played in your school gym instead of a market square, which panel would you change, and why?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Describe what Amara is doing in one sentence. Use an exact verb.
2
What is Kwesi holding?
Look at the picture. Describe what Kwesi holds in one sentence. Name the object exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Describe the teacher's action in one sentence. Use an exact verb.
4
Where are these students? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Describe this place in one sentence. Name it exactly, not “a room.”
5
Tell me about the storyboard.
Look at the picture. Describe the board in one sentence. Use exact nouns, not “things.”
6
What is Zuri wearing?
Look at the picture. Describe Zuri's clothing in one sentence. Use the exact color and item.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CA VAPA Theatre Re9c — Formulate a deeper understanding and appreciation of a drama/theatre work by considering its specific purpose or intended audience. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
